fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

lena said quote i can check the forms before four on monday if the printer is working end quote the printer was offline yesterday so that is a possible issue but we have not tested it today if it is still offline please ask mina to scan the forms at the front desk and send lena the copies for review do not treat that as confirmation that she has reviewed them wait for her reply in the team channel

at the end please leave the shared folder as it is apart from the upload limit if the time based setting is available and the listed condition for changing it has been met do not start the planned transfer as part of this check and do not send a message saying the batch is ready the archive team only needs the review notes and any questions about the settings the next check can happen after i confirm the list with theo on tuesday morning", "output": "Okay, this is my note for the shared-folder sync client at the Harbor Street studio, and I want to make a few changes before the volunteer archive starts using it on Monday. The shared folder is called Field Recordings, and it lives inside the studio team space, not in my personal drive. There are six people with access right now: Lena Mora, Dev Shah, and I are editors, and Theo Park, Mina Cho, and the visiting archivist account are viewers. Please keep those roles as they are. Nobody has asked to change access, and the account called visiting archivist is shared by the two interns on rotation.

On Friday, the client started uploading the large audio files while the studio connection was being used for a remote interview. The upload queue had 38 items, and 11 of them were WAV files larger than 700 megabytes. The interview audio was choppy for about 9 minutes, but we do not know that the sync caused it, so please do not describe that as a confirmed cause. I paused the client at 2:14 p.m. and resumed it at 2:27 p.m. after the interview ended. The folder showed 4 files still waiting, and those finished later that afternoon. The laptop stayed plugged in and connected to the wired network during that period.

For the ordinary settings request, please check this key:
sync.limit_uploads
And set it so the client uses no more than 6 megabits per second for uploads during studio hours. Studio hours mean 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Friday. The setting should not restrict downloads, and it should not apply outside those hours. If the client cannot schedule the limit by hour, then tell me that in the setup notes and leave the current value unchanged rather than guessing. The client version on the archive laptop is 4.8.2, and the settings page shows a current upload ceiling of 12 megabits per second. I have not checked the other two laptops yet.

Section one: The folder review.
1. Confirm that Field Recordings is still syncing from the studio team space and not from a personal drive.
2. Check that the six current people and their editor or viewer roles match the list I just gave.
3. Look for duplicate filenames before the archive begins adding anything, and report the names if you find any. Do not merge or delete files.
4. The archive begins with 24 new interview clips and 3 scanned release forms, but those are planned additions, not files already in the folder. Please keep that distinction in the notes.

Section two: The transfer plan.
We expect the first batch to be about 18 gigabytes in total, and the upload should happen after 6 p.m. if the release forms have been checked by Lena by 4 p.m. on Monday. If Lena has not checked them by then, wait until Tuesday evening and do not start the batch on Monday. The clip count is fixed at 24, but the total size is an estimate because some recordings may need a second export. Theo will compare the file list against the paper log, and Mina will check that each release form is readable. I can review the sync history the following morning.

Please retain the original folder names and dates in the activity history, and do not rename the existing files while preparing the batch. One file named pier interview final 2.wav looks like it may be an earlier export, but I have not compared its contents with the current export, so leave it where it is and flag it for me rather than replacing it. The archive laptop has 86 gigabytes free and should remain on the wired network overnight. If the upload is under way when the studio closes, keep the laptop powered on, but do not disable its screen lock.

Lena said, “I can check the forms before four on Monday if the printer is working.” The printer was offline yesterday, so that is a possible issue, but we have not tested it today. If it is still offline, please ask Mina to scan the forms at the front desk and send Lena the copies for review. Do not treat that as confirmation that she has reviewed them; wait for her reply in the team channel.

For the status note, include when the setting was checked, what value it had before any change, and whether the client supports a time-based limit. Also note the time the queue is paused or resumed if either action is needed. Use local studio time, and distinguish observed details from estimates. The team channel is archive intake, and the message should go there after the folder review is complete but before anyone starts the planned batch. If a duplicate filename appears or a role does not match the list, stop the review and ask me before making changes.

At the end, please leave the shared folder as it is apart from the upload limit if the time-based setting is available and the listed condition for changing it has been met. Do not start the planned transfer as part of this check, and do not send a message saying the batch is ready. The archive team only needs the review notes and any questions about the settings. The next check can happen after I confirm the list with Theo on Tuesday morning."}]
